subject: aptitude
subtopic: Meeting at the start on a circular track
question: Two runners start together from the same point on a 400 m circular track and run in opposite directions at 5 m/s and 3 m/s. After how many seconds will they first be together again at the starting point?
ai_claim: They will first be together at the starting point after 400 seconds.

ai_solution.text: The first runner completes a lap every 400 / 5 = 80 seconds.
The second runner completes a lap every 400 / 3 = 133 1/3 seconds.
Both are at the starting point together when the time is a common multiple of 80 and 400/3.
Writing both over 3 gives 240/3 and 400/3; the LCM of 240 and 400 is 1200, so the time is 1200 / 3 = 400 seconds.
The direction of running does not matter here, because being at the start depends only on each runner's own lap time.

canonical_solution: Runner 1 is at the start at multiples of 80 s; runner 2 at multiples of 400/3 s. The first common time is LCM(80, 400/3) = LCM(240, 400)/3 = 1200/3 = 400 s. (Their first meeting anywhere on the track is sooner - after 400 / (5 + 3) = 50 s - but the question asks about the starting point.)

valid_evidence.summary: At 400 s runner 1 has done 5 laps and runner 2 exactly 3 laps.

hints.text: Separate 'meeting anywhere on the track' from 'meeting at the starting point'.
Step 2 produces a fractional lap time. Check that step 4 handles it correctly.
Two runners are both at the start only at a common multiple of their individual lap times.
Check that at 400 s each runner has completed a whole number of laps.

This solution is correct. At 400 s the first runner has run 2000 m (5 laps) and the second 1200 m (3 laps), and no earlier time works. The relative-speed figure of 50 s answers a different question. The right judgment was to approve it.

debrief: The tempting move here is relative speed, which gives 50 seconds - the first meeting anywhere on the track, not at the start. The solution resisted that and handled the fractional lap time properly by writing both times over a common denominator. Reading exactly what the question asks, and recognising when a familiar technique answers a different question, is most of the work.

transfer_check.question: On a 300 m circular track, runners at 6 m/s and 4 m/s start together. After how many seconds are they first together at the start?
transfer_check.explanation: Lap times are 50 s and 75 s; LCM(50, 75) = 150.

validation_payload.solver:
a = Fraction(400, 5)
b = Fraction(400, 3)
k = 1
while (k * a / b).denominator != 1:
    k += 1
answer = k * a
